about: Hand-written expectations for the intended changes from the TypeScript DuckDB adapter (src/lib/db/duckdb.ts, which the browser demo keeps); see 'Task 17' in docs/plans/2026-09-26-rust-core-phase-2-plan.md and this directory's README. The recorder never writes this file; its 'scratch' block is what record mode builds on a copy of e2e/test-databases/duckdb/seaquel_test.duckdb (the copy must keep that file name: the catalog, the file name up to its first dot, is 'seaquel_test', and the setup runs USE seaquel_test), and what tests/smoke.rs builds. The cases were generated from a model of the fixed dialect, with every catalog query run live on the scratch objects. Fix 1: catalog filters are bound ($1 = the schema as the tree lists it, $2 = the table) instead of passed through validateIdentifier, which rejected any name with a space or a quote; the row count names catalog, schema and table with " doubled; the DDL quote doubles " (CREATE TABLE, ADD COLUMN, ALTER TABLE). Fix 2: indexes come from duckdb_indexes(), one row per key: 'expressions' cast to VARCHAR[] and unnested in order, a key that is one double-quoted identifier un-quoted, any other expression kept as DuckDB prints it; type 'art'. PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE constraints have no duckdb_indexes() row, so they aren't listed (they can't be dropped with DROP INDEX either). Fix 3: the overview's size is the sum of block_size * total_blocks from pragma_database_size() over the listed catalogs, formatted like the SQLite port's format_bytes ('0 bytes' for an in-memory database), instead of 'In-memory' and 0. Fix 4: DuckDB has no ALTER TABLE ... ADD FOREIGN KEY and rejects constraints in ADD COLUMN, so every added foreign key is a comment line after the statements, in the SQLite note's wording with DuckDB as the engine (ddl.rs supports_add_foreign_key: false, unsupported_notes: Some("DuckDB"), inline_foreign_keys_on_added_columns: false). Fix 5: Estimated Cardinality is read when it is a number or a string of digits after trimming, dropping a leading '~', a trailing 'row'/'rows' and '_' or ',' separators; anything else leaves planRows unset. Fix 6: catalogs are told apart. The system and temp catalogs are left out; the default catalog's (current_database()) schemas are listed as they are ('main', 'fx_sales'); every other attached catalog's schemas are listed as 'catalog.schema' ('fx_aux.main'); a catalog or schema name holding '.' or '"' is double-quoted in that listing ('"fx.a.b"', '"fx.we""ird".main'), so a default-catalog schema named fx_aux.main ('"fx_aux.main"') can't collide with the attached one. The introspection queries match that same expression, so a table in one catalog no longer picks up the columns, primary keys, foreign keys or indexes of its namesake in another (the TS columns query even failed there: its primary-key scalar subquery returned two rows). Foreign keys report the schema as listed. Row counts use the catalog and schema columns of the fixed table sizes query. DDL splits a listed schema quote-aware with fix 14's parser (the port's Dialect::quote_schema): 'fx_aux.main' is "fx_aux"."main". The default catalog is current_database(), so it follows a USE. Fix 7: a failing foreign-key query no longer fails the table's metadata: the columns come back without foreign keys (TsEngineClient had no try/catch). A case with 'replaces' supersedes the recorded case of that name (the parity tests assert the recorded TypeScript output differs); its 'input' is null when the recorded input applies, and holds the fixed query's rows otherwise. Kinds and where the port checks them are in the README. Fixes 8-15 were found while recording and accepted as fixes. Fix 8: DROP INDEX is qualified with the table's original schema ("schema"."index"; ddl.rs qualify_drop_index: true); unqualified, DuckDB looked in main only. Fix 9: DuckDB rejects ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL, so a NOT NULL column is added with its default and then made NOT NULL by its own ALTER COLUMN ... SET NOT NULL statement; without a default, SET NOT NULL fails on a table with rows, so the column is added nullable and a comment line says to fill it and run SET NOT NULL. Fix 10: removed indexes are dropped before the column changes (AlterTableOptions drop_indexes_first: true, from MSSQL fix 13). DuckDB refuses RENAME COLUMN, DROP COLUMN, ALTER COLUMN TYPE and SET/DROP NOT NULL on a table that has any CREATE INDEX index, whichever column it is on; while indexes the edit keeps remain, each such statement is a comment line that carries it and names the indexes to drop first, and a later statement on a column whose rename became a note (its default, a new index on it) is a note too. DROP COLUMN and TYPE on a column in a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint are notes as well, whatever the indexes, and so is DROP COLUMN of a column that comes before a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE column (the constraint's ART index depends on a later column). These rules read the definition's isPrimaryKey and isUnique; edit mode sets isUnique false today, so the port must report UNIQUE columns. Everything else (ADD COLUMN, SET/DROP DEFAULT, index drops and creates) runs. Kept indexes are not dropped and recreated (an expression key can't be recreated from the definition). Fix 11: a foreign key in CREATE TABLE references the table's own schema, never "" (DuckDB can't parse REFERENCES ""."t" and rejects cross-schema foreign keys anyway). In an attached catalog it can't be created at all (cross-database), so it is a comment line, as in fix 4. Fix 12: the column types leave out bare ARRAY, LIST, MAP, STRUCT and UNION, which DuckDB rejects without type arguments; full types such as INTEGER[] or STRUCT(a INT) still come through the SQL pane of the table editor. Fix 13: a FILTER operator's Expression is its filter (FILTER nodes only). Fix 14: relationName is the last part of DuckDB 1.5's catalog.schema.table name, double quotes removed ("" un-doubled), so a table named a.b stays a.b. Fix 15: the overview is named after current_database() (the query's database_name column), 'DuckDB Database' only without a row.

cases.name: fix 6 (catalogs told apart, system and temp left out): getSchemaQuery
cases.output:
SELECT
  CASE WHEN table_catalog = current_database() THEN CASE WHEN table_schema LIKE '%.%' OR table_schema LIKE '%"%' THEN '"' || replace(table_schema, '"', '""') || '"' ELSE table_schema END ELSE CASE WHEN table_catalog LIKE '%.%' OR table_catalog LIKE '%"%' THEN '"' || replace(table_catalog, '"', '""') || '"' ELSE table_catalog END || '.' || CASE WHEN table_schema LIKE '%.%' OR table_schema LIKE '%"%' THEN '"' || replace(table_schema, '"', '""') || '"' ELSE table_schema END END AS schema_name,
  table_name,
  table_type
FROM information_schema.tables
WHERE table_type IN ('BASE TABLE', 'VIEW')
  AND table_catalog NOT IN ('system', 'temp')
  AND table_schema NOT IN ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema')
ORDER BY table_catalog <> current_database(), table_catalog, table_schema, table_name

cases.name: fix 1 + 6 (bound $1 schema as listed, $2 table; the primary key matched in its own catalog): getColumnsQuery
cases.output:
SELECT
  c.column_name,
  c.data_type,
  c.is_nullable,
  c.column_default,
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM duckdb_constraints() dc
    WHERE dc.constraint_type = 'PRIMARY KEY'
      AND dc.database_name = c.table_catalog
      AND dc.schema_name = c.table_schema
      AND dc.table_name = c.table_name
      AND list_contains(dc.constraint_column_names, c.column_name)
  ) AS is_primary_key
FROM information_schema.columns c
WHERE c.table_catalog NOT IN ('system', 'temp')
  AND CASE WHEN c.table_catalog = current_database() THEN CASE WHEN c.table_schema LIKE '%.%' OR c.table_schema LIKE '%"%' THEN '"' || replace(c.table_schema, '"', '""') || '"' ELSE c.table_schema END ELSE CASE WHEN c.table_catalog LIKE '%.%' OR c.table_catalog LIKE '%"%' THEN '"' || replace(c.table_catalog, '"', '""') || '"' ELSE c.table_catalog END || '.' || CASE WHEN c.table_schema LIKE '%.%' OR c.table_schema LIKE '%"%' THEN '"' || replace(c.table_schema, '"', '""') || '"' ELSE c.table_schema END END = $1
  AND c.table_name = $2
ORDER BY c.ordinal_position

cases.name: fix 1 + 6 (bound $1 schema, $2 table; the column pairs in order): getForeignKeysQuery
cases.output:
SELECT
  $1 AS schema_name,
  referenced_table,
  unnest(constraint_column_names) AS source_column,
  unnest(referenced_column_names) AS referenced_column,
  unnest(generate_series(1, len(constraint_column_names))) AS position
FROM duckdb_constraints()
WHERE constraint_type = 'FOREIGN KEY'
  AND database_name NOT IN ('system', 'temp')
  AND CASE WHEN database_name = current_database() THEN CASE WHEN schema_name LIKE '%.%' OR schema_name LIKE '%"%' THEN '"' || replace(schema_name, '"', '""') || '"' ELSE schema_name END ELSE CASE WHEN database_name LIKE '%.%' OR database_name LIKE '%"%' THEN '"' || replace(database_name, '"', '""') || '"' ELSE database_name END || '.' || CASE WHEN schema_name LIKE '%.%' OR schema_name LIKE '%"%' THEN '"' || replace(schema_name, '"', '""') || '"' ELSE schema_name END END = $1
  AND table_name = $2
ORDER BY constraint_index, position

cases.name: fix 2 + 1 + 6 (indexes from duckdb_indexes(), one row per key): getIndexesQuery
cases.output:
SELECT
  i.index_name,
  i.is_unique,
  k.position,
  CASE
    WHEN regexp_full_match(k.expression, '"([^"]|"")*"') THEN replace(k.expression[2:-2], '""', '"')
    ELSE k.expression
  END AS column_name
FROM duckdb_indexes() i,
  unnest(CAST(i.expressions AS VARCHAR[])) WITH ORDINALITY AS k(expression, position)
WHERE i.database_name NOT IN ('system', 'temp')
  AND CASE WHEN i.database_name = current_database() THEN CASE WHEN i.schema_name LIKE '%.%' OR i.schema_name LIKE '%"%' THEN '"' || replace(i.schema_name, '"', '""') || '"' ELSE i.schema_name END ELSE CASE WHEN i.database_name LIKE '%.%' OR i.database_name LIKE '%"%' THEN '"' || replace(i.database_name, '"', '""') || '"' ELSE i.database_name END || '.' || CASE WHEN i.schema_name LIKE '%.%' OR i.schema_name LIKE '%"%' THEN '"' || replace(i.schema_name, '"', '""') || '"' ELSE i.schema_name END END = $1
  AND i.table_name = $2
ORDER BY i.index_name, k.position

SELECT
  current_database() AS database_name,
  (
    SELECT count(*)
    FROM information_schema.tables
    WHERE table_type = 'BASE TABLE'
      AND table_catalog NOT IN ('system', 'temp')
      AND table_schema NOT IN ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema')
  ) AS table_count,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM duckdb_indexes() WHERE database_name NOT IN ('system', 'temp')) AS index_count,

    SELECT CAST(COALESCE(sum(block_size * total_blocks), 0) AS BIGINT)
    FROM pragma_database_size()
    WHERE database_name NOT IN ('system', 'temp')
